# Current-time AC OCSP fixture

`ocsp-alice-role-with-rev-2028-02-01.der` is an AA-signed response generated by pinned Certomancer 0.16.0 for the same AC and issuer as the unchanged 2020 signing fixture. Its SHA-256 is `d30e61620a051faa16c4385a856e2c212befd1ae388ab7dfe761fac3d7fed1a4`. Generation checks the actual public AC/AA/root bytes, exact CertID and issuer signature; `ocsp-2028-source.json` preserves the source pins.

The P7 caller adapter must provide responses at the requested validation time. It originally returned the static 2020 response even for a 2028 request. Native validation correctly rejected that stale evidence. The corrected test adapter returns this fixture only for the unchanged 2028 validation context; production clocks, mandatory revocation requirements and context contents are unchanged. A separate negative control deliberately returns the 2020 response at 2028 and requires the authenticated role to be absent with a freshness error.

Regenerate with the pinned oracle interpreter and public inputs retained by `SIGIS_P7_ARTIFACT_DIR`:

```sh
/tmp/pyhanko-oracle/venv/bin/python crates/testdata/data/lanes/r3-p/ac/generate_ocsp_2028.py --inputs <retained-case-directory> --out <output-directory>
```

The generator never changes the 2020 fixture or embeds a new private key. Fixture generation is not an upstream-function pass or a full validation result. The native adapter uses replayed PKI evidence; its backend labels alone do not prove independent HTTP implementations.
